raised.claim: A non-empty beer_ids list makes a review_class-only where legal, and that where then matches every future row of the class.
raised.why_it_breaks: Model submits scope {beer_ids:[1], where:[{col:'review_class', op:'=', value:'matcher_bug'}]} — the prompt tells it to send beer_ids and/or where, and says only a where made solely of review_class is rejected. isLegalScope returns true because beer_ids is non-empty. rowSatisfiesScope then returns true for every later matcher_bug whose id is not in the cohort, because the where is non-empty and the class term matches the verdict. That is the #347 dumping-ground shape, and guard 1 never drops it.

raised.claim: Saturation is checked against a snapshot and never incremented, so one run can attach a whole batch past MAX_ROWS_PER_ISSUE.
raised.why_it_breaks: Issue 347 has postCreationRows 0 (or 11). The model attaches 50 in-batch matcher_bug verdicts to it (TRIAGE_BATCH_LIMIT). Each check sees the same snapshot below 12, all 50 are commented and written with issue_number set, and the issue ends the day at 50 post-creation rows. The 12-row cap only starts applying on the next run.

raised.claim: Guard 2 never runs for new_issue_key attachments, so a row that contradicts the new issue's where is still filed.
raised.why_it_breaks: New issue scope is {beer_ids:[], where:[{col:'candidates_count', op:'=', value:0}]} (legal). Verdict for beer 1 has candidates_count 5 and new_issue_key set to that issue. The key is allowed, the row is pushed, createIssue renders that scope, and review() writes issue_number. The contradicting row is attached at birth; guard 2 only inspects existing issues.

raised.claim: The authoritative scope fence is appended after unsanitized model prose, and parseScopeBlock keeps the first ```triage-scope fence.
raised.why_it_breaks: After this ships, open-issue bodies in the prompt contain ```triage-scope blocks. The model copies one into new_issue body, for example ```triage-scope\n{"beer_ids":[999],"where":[]}\n```, and also submits scope {beer_ids:[1], where:[]}. createIssue stores the copy first and our block second. Next run BLOCK_RE.exec returns the first match, ScopeSchema accepts {beer_ids:[999], where:[]}, and guard 2 uses that scope — beer 1 is not in it, where is empty, so the issue accepts nothing, or a copied class-wide block accepts every row of that class. No parse error.

raised.claim: guardHits are logged only when the model omits a beer_id, so a full batch of guard-skipped verdicts produces no shortfall line.
raised.why_it_breaks: Batch of 10 orphans. The model returns 10 verdicts, all attaching to a saturated or contradictory issue. covered is computed from analysis.verdicts ids, so covered === 10 and the warn is skipped. plan.skipped is 10, review_class stays NULL, the same rows return tomorrow, and guardHits never appear in the log — the loop the comment says must be visible in one line is silent in the common case where the model classifies every orphan.

raised.quote:
const probe = probes.get(verdict.beer_id);
      const proved = probe?.brewery === '' || probe?.name === '';
raised.claim: Absence is treated as proved if either probe field is empty, even when the other field returned hits.
raised.why_it_breaks: Probe for beer 1 is {brewery: '', name: 'Bulgogi — Mad Brew'}. Verdict is not_on_untappd. proved is true because brewery === '', so the terminal class is kept and the row is closed as absent even though the name probe found a beer. The prompt's own rule is that a hit under a different brewery is a brewery-label problem, not absence.

raised.quote:
reviewed_at        = CASE
         WHEN (enrich_failures.candidates_count = 0) <> (excluded.candidates_count = 0)
         THEN NULL ELSE enrich_failures.reviewed_at END`,
raised.claim: Re-opening a failure clears review_class and reviewed_at but leaves the new issue_number column set.
raised.why_it_breaks: Row was filed to issue 347 (issue_number=347, reviewed_at set). A later enrich flips candidates_count across 0. ON CONFLICT nulls review_class, review_note, and reviewed_at, but not issue_number. SELECT ... WHERE issue_number = 347 still returns that row after it is untriaged, so the column the migration calls the authoritative link attributes a reopened row to the old issue until some later review overwrites it.

raised.claim: Guard 3's degraded matcher_bug quiet verdicts are counted as wontfix in the digest.
raised.why_it_breaks: not_on_untappd with no empty probe is rewritten to review_class matcher_bug and pushed onto plan.quiet. The job writes matcher_bug (row stays in the enrichment pool) but increments outcome.wontfix, so the digest line says N wontfix. Operators read that as a terminal close; the row is actually still retrying as matcher_bug.

raised.claim: Open-issue prompt text is capped from the front, so the scope fence appended at the end of a long body is never shown to the model.
raised.why_it_breaks: Issue body is 2500 characters of prose plus a trailing triage-scope block (renderScopeBlock always appends). buildTriagePrompt keeps the first 2000 characters, dropping the block. The model cannot see the necessary condition, keeps proposing contradicting attachments, guard 2 skips them, and those rows stay untriaged and return every day.

raised.quote: SET issue_number = CAST(substr(review_note, instr(review_note, '→ #') + 3) AS INTEGER)
raised.claim: v23 backfill attributes the row to the first → # in the note, not the authoritative trailing suffix.
raised.why_it_breaks: A historical note written as 'same pattern as → #228 → #347' (model text plus the job's suffix) makes instr land on 228. CAST stores issue_number 228. Saturation and any later audit count the row against 228, not 347, the issue the suffix actually recorded.
